featured_reviews.review_text:
Updated: This review is subjective, because I had joined the classes (1 month verbal crash course) around 11th November, about 1.5 months before my actual GMAT. and I had also taken only one test offered in the class. (out of 5-6)  Additionally, I had not attended the Quant classes , but had access to few online questions. The questions for Quant looked good, but please use your judgment and maybe do a trial beforehand.
This was the first result from a simple google search for GMAT classes in Mumbai. But overall the classes didn't help me much. There were many important topics which I think weren't covered in the class. Topics such as idioms for sentence correction were not discussed,  practice on "sentence meaning" in sentence correction, techniques in RC were not taught, and for CR techniques like the negation technique in Assumptions and the yes/no technique for evaluation were taught, but reasoning , cause-effect, and practice on hard questions was not sufficient. Practice was provided for major CR type questions though.Resources given were several homework sheets and to do in class sheets,  verbal question bank ( 200 questions, but more like grammar practice), and online tests. The online verbal practice material was easier compared to the actual GMAT and the GMAT prep software. The exercises for basic grammar were okay, but they are not enough for a hard sentence correction question.

Overall, it gave me a start for my studies, but covering major topics and finding tough questions was something I had to do on my own, I realized that after giving GMAT. I had joined the classes presuming that I can give gmat in 1.5 month after completing a 1 month crash course(20hrs) using this class; however, now I have realized that if the amount I had spent for these classes (~20k Rs), had been spent to do self study using books and online tests ( Powerscore CR bible, Manhattan SC guide, Aristotle SC grail, Manhattan RC guide) with a little more time given to self study, then my GMAT results could have been better. I relied too much on these classes which could also be a mistake. This review could be true for all verbal crash course gmat experiences. Hence, I suggest please use your own judgemnet. featured_reviews.name: Kushagra Nath
featured_reviews.review_text:
I joined TIME Churchgate for the CAT 2024 classes, and they truly played a significant role in my exam and interview preparation. The sessions provided valuable insights into how one should prepare for the exam and work towards achieving the desired percentile . The GDPI classes taught me how present myself during interviews and also kept me well-informed on current affairs.
Apart from this what I really found useful were the AIMCAT mocks which made me realise the importance of consistency and practice.

featured_reviews.name: Ammar Savliwala
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a great experience with TIME coaching for CAT 2024. The teaching quality is excellent, with experienced faculty, vast study material and regular mock exams (AIMCATS) which helps in syllabus completion and overall performance. The mentoring sessions taken at the churchgate and dadar branches were especially helpful in identifying and working on my weak areas, giving me a clear direction to improve. Highly recommended for serious CAT aspirants!
